claims.text: Optimized PBF-LB/M processing that induces rapid solidification will refine the microstructure of WMoTaNbV.
Optimized PBF-LB/M processing will produce a high density of nanoscale twins in WMoTaNbV.
The PBF-LB/M-induced microstructure will increase the yield strength of WMoTaNbV relative to conventionally processed material.
The PBF-LB/M-induced microstructure will improve or maintain the ductility of WMoTaNbV relative to conventionally processed material.
Conventionally processed WMoTaNbV typically has a coarser grain structure than the proposed PBF-LB/M material.
Conventionally processed WMoTaNbV typically has a lower twin density than the proposed PBF-LB/M material.
Conventionally processed WMoTaNbV typically has a moderate dislocation density.
Tailoring laser scanning speed, energy density, and cooling rate can promote rapid solidification in WMoTaNbV.
The proposed processing strategy can achieve near-full densification exceeding 99%.
The proposed processing will increase the dislocation density of WMoTaNbV.
Rapid solidification produces high thermal gradients and residual stresses in the alloy.
High thermal gradients and residual stresses promote nanoscale twin nucleation during cooling.
The refined microstructure impedes dislocation movement.
The combined effects of nanoscale twins and increased dislocation density improve the strength-plasticity balance.
The predicted improvement will occur only within a narrowly defined PBF-LB/M processing window.
Processing conditions that generate excessive residual stress may cause defects or embrittlement.
